While n is greater than 0, add the last digit to the sum, then remove it with integer division.

title: Finding a maximum
Count even numbers
statement: N and then N integers are given. Print how many are even.
hints: Read N first, then read exactly N numbers in a loop.
Inside the loop test each value with the remainder operator and increment a counter.

title: Sum and average
statement: N and then N integers are given. Print the sum and the average (decimal) separated by a space.
hints: Keep a running sum while reading, and divide at the end.
Cast the sum to double (or divide by a decimal) before dividing by N so the average keeps its fraction.

title: Reverse a number (bug)
statement: This program should reverse the number N (1234 -> 4321, 1200 -> 21) but it is wrong. Fix it.
hints: Trace the loop for 123 and watch what happens to n after the first pass.
Compare how the loop treats the digit it has just used with how the sum-of-digits loop treats it. Does n actually get shorter on each pass?

title: Collatz steps
statement:
A number n > 0 is given. Until n = 1: if n is even do n/2, otherwise 3n+1. Print how many steps are needed. (6 -> 8 steps; 1 -> 0 steps)
Here n < 100000, so all intermediate values fit in an int.
hints: Use a while loop that runs until n reaches its final value and count each iteration.
Each pass applies one of two rules depending on a property of n, and counts one step either way.

title: GCD (Euclid)
statement: Two positive integers a and b are given on one line. Find and print their greatest common divisor using Euclid's algorithm (inside a while loop).
hints: Euclid's algorithm repeatedly replaces the pair by a smaller pair using a remainder, until one number becomes 0.
Be careful about the order of updates: do not overwrite a value you still need. Decide which variable holds the answer at the end.

title: Counting with a condition
Minimum
statement: N and then N integers are given. Print the smallest.
hints: Start with the first number as the minimum, then compare the remaining ones.
Read the first value before the loop; loop N - 1 more times and replace the minimum whenever a smaller value shows up.

title: Longest run
statement: N and then N integers are given. Print the length of the longest run of equal consecutive numbers.
hints: Track the length of the current run and the best length seen so far.
Remember the previous number. If the new number equals it, add 1 to the run, otherwise reset the run to 1; update the best each pass.

title: Maximum of negatives
statement: The program should print the largest of N numbers but it fails when all numbers are negative. Fix it.
hints: Check what max starts as. Would it work if every input were negative?
The starting value must not be able to beat a real input. Which actual value could you start from?

Sum of digits (trace)
FRQ: Parking garage fees
statement:
A parking garage charges by the length of a visit.
- The first 30 minutes are free.
- After that, the charge is 2 dollars for every 15 minutes or part of 15 minutes (31 to 45 minutes costs 2 dollars, 46 minutes costs 4 dollars).
- The charge for one visit never exceeds 20 dollars.

Write the class Garage.

(a) Write the method int fee(int minutes), which returns the charge in dollars for one visit of the given number of minutes (minutes >= 0).

(b) Write the method int totalFee(int firstMinutes, int visits). Visit number k (k = 0, 1, ..., visits - 1) lasts firstMinutes + 10 * k minutes. The method returns the total charge for all visits. Your method must call fee. If visits is 0, return 0.

Examples: fee(20) returns 0, fee(31) returns 2, fee(46) returns 4. totalFee(20, 3) covers visits of 20, 30 and 40 minutes and returns 2.

This question is in the style of AP Exam Free-Response Question 1 (Methods and Control Structures). Use only the Java features from this course. You may write any helper code you need.
hints: In (a) handle the free period first, then count how many 15-minute blocks (rounding up) come after it, and cap the charge.
To round up a division by 15 with integers, add 14 before dividing. In (b), loop over the visits and call fee on each duration, adding to a total.

title: FRQ: Digit sums
statement:
Write the class DigitTools.

(a) Write the static method int digitSum(int n), which returns the sum of the decimal digits of n (n >= 0). For example, digitSum(9875) returns 29 and digitSum(1000) returns 1.

(b) Write the static method int countWithDigitSum(int lo, int hi, int target), which returns how many integers n with lo <= n <= hi (lo >= 0) have digitSum(n) equal to target. Your method must call digitSum. If lo > hi, return 0.

Example: countWithDigitSum(1, 20, 3) returns 2 (the numbers 3 and 12).

This question is in the style of AP Exam Free-Response Question 1 (Methods and Control Structures). Use only the Java features from this course. You may write any helper code you need.
hints: Part (a) peels off digits with % and /. Part (b) loops over the range and calls digitSum.
In (b), initialise a counter, loop n from lo to hi, and increment the counter when digitSum(n) equals target. A loop with lo > hi naturally never runs.

title: Palindromic number
statement: A positive integer N is given. Without using Strings, print YES if the number equals its reverse, otherwise NO.
hints: Build the reversed number digit by digit, keeping a copy of the original.
Save n before the loop. Then peel off the last digit of n and append it to the reversed number, and finally compare with the saved copy.

title: Count the primes
statement: N is given. Print how many primes are at most N.
hints: Use an outer loop over candidates and an inner loop that looks for a divisor.
For each candidate from 2 to N, assume it is prime and set a flag to false if some divisor d with d * d at most the candidate divides it.

title: Perfect numbers
statement: N is given. Print how many perfect numbers are at most N. (A perfect number equals the sum of its proper divisors, e.g. 6 = 1 + 2 + 3.)
hints: For each number add up its proper divisors, then compare the sum with the number.
An outer loop over the candidates and an inner loop over possible divisors; reset the sum for each candidate.

title: Is 1 prime?
statement: The program should print YES for primes only, but it says YES for 1. Fix it.
hints: Trace the program for the input 1: which values does the flag go through?
The flag starts as true. Which numbers should never be reported as prime, and how can the starting value reflect that?

title: Trailing zeros of a factorial
statement:
Print how many zeros are at the end of N!. 1 <= N <= 1,000,000,000 (you cannot compute N!, think!).
Hint: each zero comes from a 2x5 pair; 5s are rarer.
hints: Each trailing zero needs a factor 10 = 2 * 5, and factors of 2 are plentiful. Count the factors of 5.
Count the multiples of 5 up to n, then the multiples of 25 (they have a second 5), then 125, and so on.

title: Most frequent digit
statement: A non-negative integer is given as text. Print the digit that appears most often (smallest digit if tied).
hints: Count how often each digit 0 to 9 occurs, remembering the best one so far.
Loop over the 10 digits; for each, scan the text and count matches. Only replace the best when the count is strictly larger, so ties keep the smaller digit.

title: Count perfect numbers
statement: n is given (1 to 10000). Print how many perfect numbers are at most n. A perfect number equals the sum of its proper divisors (6 = 1 + 2 + 3).
hints: Sum the proper divisors of each number up to n and compare.
Use a nested loop where the inner loop collects the divisors of the current candidate; reset your total each time.

title: Multiplicative persistence
statement: A non-negative integer n is given (it fits in an int). Repeatedly replace n by the product of its digits until n has a single digit. Print how many replacements were needed. (39 -> 27 -> 14 -> 4 takes 3.)
hints: Use an outer loop that repeats while n has at least two digits, and an inner loop that combines the digits.
Each outer pass builds a new number from the digits of the old one and counts a step; think about the right starting value for the combined result.

title: Longest run of equal digits
statement: A non-negative integer is given as text. Print the length of the longest block of consecutive equal digits.
hints: Compare each character with the one before it, tracking the current run length and the best length.
Start both run and best at 1. For each index from 1, compare the one-letter substring with the one before it; extend or reset the run, and update the best.

title: Reverse a word
statement: A single word is given. Print its letters in reverse order. (java -> avaj)
hints: Walk through the word from the last index down to 0 and build a new String.
Start the loop at the last valid index, decrease the index, and append the one-letter substring at each index.

title: Counting a letter
Building a reverse
Count the s letters
statement: Count how many times s appears in Mississippi (4).
hints: Each pass compares a one-letter substring with a String.
The blank is a String literal for the letter you count, so it must be in double quotes.

title: Count a letter
statement: A word and a letter are given. Print how many times the letter appears.
hints: Visit every position, take a one-letter substring and compare with the letter.
Use equals (not ==) to compare Strings, and increase a counter on a match.

title: Vowel counter
statement: The program should count the vowels (a e i o u) in the word but it throws an error. Fix it.
hints: The exception means an index went out of range. Check the loop bounds.
Compare the largest index the loop can reach with the last valid index of the String.

title: Palindromic word
statement: A single word is given. Print YES if the word equals its reverse, otherwise NO.
hints: Compare letters from both ends moving toward the middle.
Letter i must equal the letter i places from the end, for every i in the first half of the word; one mismatch means NO.

title: Filtering characters
Palindrome check
Remove vowels
statement: A lowercase word is given. Print it without its vowels (a e i o u).
hints: Build a new String, adding only the letters that are not vowels.
A String of all vowels together with indexOf can tell you whether a letter is a vowel: a result of -1 means it is not.

title: Capitalize
statement: A lowercase word is given. Print it with the first letter in uppercase.
hints: Use two alphabet Strings, one lowercase and one uppercase, and match positions.
Find the position of the first letter in the lowercase alphabet, take the letter at that position from the uppercase one, and add the rest of the word.

title: Index out of range
statement: The program should reverse the word but it throws an exception. Fix it.
hints: A String of length n has valid indexes 0 to n - 1. Where does the loop start?
Compare the first index the loop uses with the last valid index of the String.

title: Reverse with substring
Count letter a in banana
Caesar cipher
statement: A shift k and then a lowercase word are given. Shift every letter k places forward in the alphabet (after z comes a) and print it. (3 abc -> def)
hints: Use a String of the alphabet; the position of a letter in it can be shifted and wrapped.
Find the letter's position with indexOf, add k, take the remainder by 26 to wrap around, and look the new letter up with substring.

title: Count occurrences
statement:
A text is given on the first line and a pattern on the second. Print how many times the pattern appears in the text, counting overlaps. (in 'aaaa', 'aa' -> 3)
Hint: compare substring(i, i + pattern.length()) with the pattern at every position i.
hints: At each start position, compare a slice of the text with the pattern.
Loop over the start positions where the pattern still fits, and compare the slice of the pattern's length with equals.

title: All substring positions
Count the words
statement: A line of words separated by single spaces is given. Print the number of words.
hints: Words are separated by single spaces, so the number of spaces tells you the number of words.
Count the space characters in the line, then add 1. Read the line with the Scanner method that reads a full line.

title: Longest word
statement: A line of words separated by single spaces is given. Print the longest word (the first one if there is a tie).
hints: Track where the current word starts and compare its length with the best so far whenever a space ends it.
Append a space to the line so the last word is also ended by a space; use a strict comparison so the first of equal-length words wins.

title: Anagrams
statement: Two words are given. Print YES if they are anagrams (same letters, same counts), otherwise NO.
hints: Two words are anagrams if every letter occurs equally often in both.
Check the lengths first; then for each letter of the first word, count it in both words, and fail on any difference.

FRQ: Count and remove substrings
statement:
Write the class StringTasks. Use only the String methods length, substring, indexOf and equals.

(a) Write the static method int countOccurrences(String str, String sub), which returns the number of non-overlapping occurrences of sub in str, found by scanning from left to right. sub is not empty. For example, countOccurrences("banana", "an") returns 2 and countOccurrences("aaaa", "aa") returns 2.

(b) Write the static method String removeAll(String str, String sub), which returns str with every non-overlapping occurrence of sub (found from left to right in one pass) removed. The text that remains is NOT searched again. For example, removeAll("banana", "an") returns "ba", and removeAll("aabb", "ab") returns "ab".

This question is in the style of AP Exam Free-Response Question 1 (Methods and Control Structures). Use only the Java features from this course. You may write any helper code you need.
hints: Use indexOf to find the next occurrence, then continue searching in the rest of the String that comes after it.
After a match, replace str by the part after the match (so matches cannot overlap). For removal, append the part before each match to a result.

title: Run-length encoding
statement: A word of lowercase letters is given. Compress consecutive equal letters as letter+count. (aaabcc -> a3b1c2)
hints: Group equal neighbours: from each start index, move forward while the letter stays the same.
Use an inner while loop to find where the block ends, append the letter and the block length, and continue from the block end.

title: Longest palindromic substring
statement: A word of at most 50 letters is given. Print the length of its longest palindromic substring.
hints: Try every substring (start and end) and test whether it reads the same backward.
Use nested loops for the start and end, an inner check that compares pairs from both ends, and record the longest length found.

title: Selective run compression
statement: A word of lowercase letters is given. Replace every block of 3 or more equal consecutive letters by the letter followed by the length of the block; shorter blocks stay as they are (aaabcc -> a3bcc, aabbb -> aab3).
hints: Find each block of equal letters like in run-length encoding, but decide how to write it afterwards.
If the block length is at least 3, append the letter and the length; otherwise append the block itself (a substring from its start to its end).

title: Star triangle
Rectangle of stars
statement: Rows r and columns c are given. Print r lines of c stars each.
hints: Use a nested loop: the outer loop counts rows, the inner loop counts columns.
Print a star in the inner loop with print, and call println once after each inner loop finishes.

title: Rows times columns
Triangle bound
statement: Print the triangle  *, **, ***  (one row per line).
hints: The inner loop prints as many stars as the current row number.
The bound is the variable of the outer loop.

title: Reusing the loop variable
Multiplication grid
statement: n is given. Print an n x n table where the cell in row i, column j is i*j (numbers separated by single spaces).
hints: Row i, column j holds i times j. Watch where spaces go.
Build each row in a String, adding a space before every entry except the first, then print the row at the end of the inner loop.

statement: n is given. Print n rows: row i contains the digit i repeated i times. (n = 3: 1, 22, 333)
hints: Row i has i copies of the digit i.
The inner loop runs from 1 to i and prints i each time; end each row with a println.

title: Pairs with a given sum
statement: T is given. Count pairs (a, b) with 1 <= a <= b <= 10 and a + b = T.
hints: Use two nested loops with a <= b so each pair is counted once.
Let the inner loop start at the value of the outer variable, and count when the sum equals the target.

title: Wrong inner bound
statement: The program should print a triangle (*, **, ***, ...) with n rows but prints a square. Fix it.
hints: The inner loop controls how many stars each row gets. What should that depend on?
The bound of the inner loop should be the current row number, not the total number of rows.

title: Triangular count (shifted inner loop)
Diagonal versus others
Right-aligned triangle
Hollow square
statement: n >= 2 is given. Print an n x n square of stars that is hollow inside (spaces inside).
hints: Decide for each cell whether it is on the border.
A cell is a star if its row is the first or last, or its column is the first or last; otherwise print a space.

title: Pythagorean triples
statement: N is given. Count triples a <= b <= c <= N with a*a + b*b = c*c.
hints: Three nested loops with a <= b <= c; count the triples that satisfy the equation.
Start b at a and c at b so every triple appears once, and compare the sum of the first two squares with the third square.

FRQ: Number staircase
statement:
Write the class Patterns.

(a) Write the static method String row(int i, int n), which returns row i (1 <= i <= n <= 9) of a staircase with n rows. Row i consists of n - i dot characters followed by the digits i, i-1, ..., 1 (no spaces). For example, row(2, 4) returns "..21" and row(4, 4) returns "4321".

(b) Write the static method String staircase(int n), which returns all n rows, in order from row 1 to row n, separated by the newline character "\n" (no newline after the last row). Your method must call row. For example, staircase(3) returns "..1\n.21\n321".

This question is in the style of AP Exam Free-Response Question 1 (Methods and Control Structures). Use only the Java features from this course. You may write any helper code you need.
hints: Row i is built from two parts: some dots, then digits counting down.
In (a) use one loop for the dots and a second loop that counts down from i to 1. In (b) call row for each i and put a newline between rows, not after the last.

title: Diamond
statement: n is given. Print a diamond of 2n-1 rows. Row i (1..n) has n-i dots followed by 2i-1 stars; then the rows mirror back down. (n = 2: .* / *** / .*)
hints: Each row is some dots followed by some stars; work out how the counts change from row to row.
Compute the row's size k (rising to n, then falling back), then print n - k dots followed by the right number of stars for k.

title: Pascal's triangle
statement: n (1 to 15) is given. Print the first n rows of Pascal's triangle, numbers separated by single spaces, one row per line. Row r (starting at 0) has r + 1 numbers; each is the previous one times (r - k) / (k + 1).
hints: Each number in a row can be computed from the previous number in the same row using the formula in the statement.
Keep a value starting at 1, append it, and then update it with integer arithmetic. Multiply first, then divide, so the division is exact.

title: What do we count?
statement: In informal run-time analysis, what do we count?
choices: How many seconds the program takes on one computer
How many lines the source file has
How many times a statement or block is executed

choices: A: about n x n times

title: Count the halvings
statement: n >= 1 is given. Print how many times n can be halved (integer division) before it becomes 1.
hints: Halve repeatedly and count until the value is no longer greater than 1.
A while loop that runs while n is above 1, halving n and increasing the counter.

title: Which loop is fastest?
statement: n = 1000. Loop A: for (i = 0; i < n; i++). Loop B: for (i = 0; i < n; i += 10). Loop C: for (i = 1; i < n; i *= 2). Which executes its body the fewest times?

title: Multiplying counter
Divisor incidences
statement: n is given. Count pairs (i, j) with 1 <= i, j <= n where j divides i. (This is exactly how many times the if-body of two nested loops would run.)
hints: Run the two nested loops and count how often the condition is true.
The condition tests whether j divides i, for all i and j from 1 to n.

title: Halving or doubling loop
Executions in a triangle
Count Pythagorean triples
statement: n is given (1 to 150). Print how many triples a <= b <= c <= n of positive integers satisfy a*a + b*b = c*c. (Three nested loops are fine: about n^3/6 steps, which is acceptable for n <= 150.)
hints: Use three nested loops with a <= b <= c and count each triple that satisfies the equation.
Start each inner loop at the outer variable so triples are not repeated, and compare the sum of two squares with the third.
